decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a niche, high-value system that fits the firm's dosimetry core; it was downgraded to a mere mention in 2019, which signals some uncertainty, but there is no clear evidence that results fell short of aspirations, so continued support is likely.
Small volume ionization chambers are staple catalog items with steady demand from small-field dosimetry and low carrying cost, so there is no performance shortfall that would trigger dropping them.
This chamber complements the firm's small-field line and keeps its own page, which suggests results meet aspirations at modest resource cost.
Standard clinical ionization chambers are core recurring-revenue products in radiotherapy quality assurance and are very unlikely to be withdrawn.
Chambers for relative dosimetry are bundled with water phantom systems, so they support the established business and do not call for problemistic search.
Thimble chambers are long-lived standard products with stable demand, and carrying them costs little relative to the firm's slack.
